question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6.75% per annum rate of interest deposited on 26 February 2024 and withdrawn on 27 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time in days = 3 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 27 (Apr) = 61 days.

Since 2024 is a leap year (366 days), Time (T) in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = (4000 × 6.75 × 1/6) ÷ 100

SI = 270 ÷ 6 = 45

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 6.75% per annum

Deposited on = 26 February 2024

Withdrawn on = 27 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 26 Feb 2024
 Deposit
 ₹4,000

 27 Apr 2024
 Withdrawal
 ₹4,045
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 T = 61 Days
 
 Rate = 6.75% p.a.
 Simple Interest = ₹45

**Calculations:**

⇒ The year 2024 is divisible by 4, meaning it is a leap year, so February has 29 days.

⇒ While calculating interest duration, the day of deposit is generally excluded, but the day of withdrawal is included.

⇒ Number of days in February = 29 − 26 = 3 days

⇒ Number of days in March = 31 days

⇒ Number of days in April = 27 days

⇒ Total Time (T) = 3 + 31 + 27 = 61 days

⇒ Since 2024 is a leap year, total days in the year = 366 days.

⇒ Time (T) in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6.75 × (1/6)) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 40 × 6.75 × (1/6)

⇒ SI = 270 ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 45

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leap Year Condition

A year divisible by 4 (and by 400 if it is a century year) is a leap year and consists of 366 days. February has 29 days in a leap year.

Counting Days for Interest

When computing simple interest between two dates, only one of the dates (either the deposit date or the withdrawal date) is counted to determine the duration.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated uniformly only on the base principal amount, whereas Compound Interest (CI) is computed on both the principal and the continuously accumulated interest.
